task_A_rubric.CORRECT: Names _sited (environment_world.gd:249-256) as the placement-validity decision symbol, correctly identifies _clear (244-246) and _track_gap (219-241) as the lower-level clearance symbols it calls, and does not name _why (259-271) as the decision function.
task_A_rubric.PARTIAL: Correctly names _sited as the decision symbol but omits one of _clear/_track_gap, or a line span is outside a 2-line tolerance.
task_A_rubric.WRONG: Names _clear, _track_gap, _why, or any other symbol as the primary placement-validity decision function, or fabricates a call relationship not present in the source.

task_B_rubric.CORRECT: All 3 required files (start_platform.gd, s_curve.gd, toy_scene.gd) present with correct enclosing symbol/line for every real call site and correct function classification (which of beam_section/channel_section, or both) per file; neither v2_track.gd nor toy_geometry_check.gd claimed as a caller of toy_geometry.gd's functions; no fabricated call site.
task_B_rubric.PARTIAL: 2 of 3 required files present, or one required file's call-site set is incomplete (e.g. only one of two functions reported for a file that calls both), with no distractor fabricated as a caller.
task_B_rubric.WRONG: v2_track.gd's local channel_section() or toy_geometry_check.gd is claimed as calling toy_geometry.gd's beam_section/channel_section, a required file is missing entirely alongside another defect, or a call site is fabricated.

scoring.scoring_method: Deterministic comparison of each run's FILES/SYMBOLS/line-span fields against the external ground truth file (c3_ground_truth.json), performed by the operator after all six live runs complete -- not by another model call.
scoring.reviewer_escalation: If a task's three conditions score inconsistently in a way deterministic comparison cannot resolve, invoke exactly one independent reviewer session for that task only, given the same frozen ground truth. Never one reviewer per run.

primary_resource_metric.name: context_load_tokens
primary_resource_metric.note: output_tokens is tracked separately as generation cost and is NOT part of the primary metric. This definition must not change after seeing results.

correctness: exact missing/incorrect fields if PARTIAL or WRONG
resource: wall_time_seconds (if reliably available from turn_duration markers)
navigation: provider_returned_chars (if deterministically measurable from the tool_result)
resource_metrics.unavailable_field_policy: Any field that cannot be reliably extracted from the transcript is recorded as the literal string "UNAVAILABLE" with a one-line reason, never estimated or interpolated.

noise_floor_reference.source: Benchmark C's own recorded resource-noise spread between two runs of an identical task on identical tooling: approximately 37%.
noise_floor_reference.usage: Any measured context_load_tokens reduction smaller than this range is treated as within noise, not as a demonstrated provider benefit, per the same standard Benchmark C2 used and explicitly declined to override.

eligibility_for_productionization: 1. The provider is actually invoked (provider_call_count >= 1) in every one of its official C3 conditions (both Task A and Task B for that provider).
2. It causes no correctness downgrade versus the corresponding C0 result on the same task (no CORRECT->PARTIAL or PARTIAL->WRONG regression attributable to the condition).
3. It shows a material context_load_tokens reduction beyond the noise_floor_reference on BOTH Task A and Task B versus C0 -- not merely one lucky run.
4. It does not introduce disproportionate tool-call or turn overhead relative to C0 (no multi-x blowup in assistant_turns or total tool calls that would offset any token savings operationally).
decision_rule.mixed_result_handling: If one provider shows a clear pass on one task and a clear fail on the other, activate contingency Task C (run order C2 -> C0 -> C1) before drawing any conclusion for that provider.
decision_rule.both_fail: If neither provider clears all four eligibility conditions across Task A and Task B: recommend productionize neither.
decision_rule.both_pass: If both providers clear eligibility: compare actual correctness/resource/tool-overhead numbers and recommend the simpler operational choice (fewer moving parts, e.g. no extra venv/runtime dependency) unless one materially outperforms the other on the primary metric.
decision_rule.do_not_force_a_winner: Mirrors Benchmark C2's own frozen rule: a result is not adjusted after the fact to manufacture a winner. Inconclusive stays inconclusive and is reported as such.

session_independence.rule: Each of the (up to) 6 C3 runs is a fresh, independent developer session/process with no conversation memory carried from any other run. No prior run's answer, transcript, or score is ever supplied to a later run.
session_independence.procedural_rule_from_c2: The benchmark prompt (with its condition-specific directive, for C1/C2) must be the FIRST conversational user message in the session, with parentUuid null. Any session where a prior turn (even an accidental paste) precedes it is INVALID_PROCEDURAL_CONTAMINATION and must be replaced with a fresh run, exactly as Benchmark C2's T3/C2 was.

stop_conditions: source tree changes between conditions (re-verify git blob hashes before and after each run)
a developer session receives the C3 ground truth (grep the transcript for the external ground-truth path or its sha256 as a leak check)
one candidate's tool leaks into another condition's session (a C0 session calls ctags_query/treesitter_query, a C1 session calls treesitter_query, etc.)
a C1/C2 session completes with zero provider calls despite the forced-use directive -- this specific run is INVALID_DIRECTIVE_NOT_FOLLOWED and must be replaced, not silently accepted as evidence
Claude Code auto-updates away from 2.1.70 between runs
an infrastructure crash invalidates more than one run in the six-run set
